Vanessa —

Thanks for the note. We have held payment pending VAT clarification. BlueRidge applied the reverse charge under Article 194 for cross-border B2B supplies, so we are treating VAT as a liability on our return. Before we can pay the net amount, our AP team needs:

1) Formal VAT evidence from Redwood (VAT registration certificate and confirmation of Redwood's selling entity)
2) A copy of the signed PO (attached) showing purchase order number and entity

We can pay the net immediately once the above is received. Otherwise, we are uncomfortable remitting the VAT portion to Redwood without proof.

I attached PO_2783 which references the BlueRidge EU purchasing entity. If you can confirm the taxable entity and share a VAT cert, I'll push through the net payment today.

Regards,

Vanessa / Aditya —

Per finance, the documentation you've provided should be sufficient for the majority of EU buyers to proceed with reverse-charge net payment. Two operational notes:

1) We need the buyer VAT ID (ideally in the PO or an email from their AP) before issuing the credit-note flow.
2) If BlueRidge delays payment >45 days we will escalate to collections and mark the account for a 30-day credit hold pending an exec resolution.

Given the strategic nature of this account, I recommend we offer a temporary concession to accelerate resolution: a one-time early-payment credit of 2% on the invoice subtotal if BlueRidge pays the net within 10 calendar days of the corrected invoice issuance. That preserves revenue while creating an incentive to clear the ledger.

If you want to escalate to leadership for sign-off, I can draft a short approval note.
